STEP 1 - Vessel type: square flat plate (white, rim band, flat centre, no inner wall).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are typically 20-30 cm; this one looks medium-large, about 25 cm across.
b) Reference: the plate spans roughly 2.3-2.5 chicken-breast-length widths (chicken pieces about 7-8 cm long in frame). Plate width ≈ 3.3 x 7.5 cm ≈ 25 cm. Both cues agree.
Final width: 25 cm, square, area ≈ 625 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Kale/greens (cooked-looking, dressed, with parmesan): covers about 20% of plate ≈ 125 cm². Mound-like, average thickness about 2 cm (peak ~4 cm). Volume ≈ 125 x 2 = 250 ml. Kale is leafy; treat as cooked/dressed greens, 0.6 g/ml → ≈ 150 g.
- Chicken breast pieces (breaded/crusted, two strips plus a bit): footprint ≈ 2 strips x 7 x 2.5 cm ≈ 35 cm², thickness 2 cm → 70 ml x 1.0 = 70 g.
- Roasted squash/acorn squash cubes (4 visible pieces, approx 3 x 3 x 2 cm each, ~0.3-0.4 of a wedge area): footprint ≈ 30 cm², thickness 2 cm → 60 ml x 0.6 = 36 g.
- Parmesan shavings: a few flakes ≈ 5 g.
- Spinach/herb garnish leaves: ≈ 5 g.

Total ≈ 266 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no clear base layer beyond the greens; no bowl depth to consider.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served):
- Dressed cooked kale with oil and cheese: ~80 kcal/100 g.
- Breaded chicken breast (cooked): ~200 kcal/100 g.
- Roasted winter squash: ~45 kcal/100 g.
- Parmesan: ~400 kcal/100 g.
- Spinach garnish: ~25 kcal/100 g.

Energy estimate: kale 150 g → 120 kcal; chicken 70 g → 140 kcal; squash 36 g → 16 kcal; parmesan 5 g → 20 kcal; spinach 5 g → 1 kcal. Total ≈ 300 kcal for about 266 g.
